task: Each source has two targets: finite2 with new response parameters, or recurrent with the original response parameters. Both targets share paid prefix controls. Private family labels and seeds appear only in the experiment protocol/results.
source: The first actual published archive supplies author practice. The remaining two published archives supply transfer; their files are loaded only after authoring stops. Preserve the earlier unsuccessful acquisition and its costs separately.
intervention: Revise a previously authored research method on four anonymous practice cases, then freeze it for eight preregistered cross-source targets. Numerical operators, prefix and episode budgets are unchanged.
controller: The author selects program edits, paid practice and publication. Each practice and transfer begins with 72 paid controls-only rows, then executes at most 12 declared program steps with 24-row fresh confirmation. All fits and observations share each episode's actual budgets. Transfer uses zero LLM calls; this is LLM-authored method execution, not online LLM selection of each action.
archive_publication: New predictors retain ordinary code, data and binary dependencies. Imported confirmed-model archives accompany them only when declared in the successful finish.reused_files. Runner logs and the undeclared candidate catalog are excluded. An unchanged directly submitted archive keeps its existing dependencies. Revisions to an inherited model publish a new candidate. A latest predictor explicitly depending on an older candidate retains that dependency, which is reported.
failure_policy: Preserve the first author phase and every paid practice. If publication fails, skip eight revised slots and run all 24 registered reference episodes. No unpublished source is substituted for the revised arm.
accounting: Earlier source acquisition, author phases and replay costs remain separate. The supplied diagnostic is charged once. New authoring and all four target arms are charged at their actual costs; unknown token usage remains unknown.
terminal_order: Publish using paid practice and fresh confirmation only. Freeze the method before loading transfer archives. Complete all transfer research before terminal scoring; no terminal outcome affects publication or target admission.
scope: Two existing archives times four conditions: unchanged, changed response, recurrent instrument, and a response change after the initial validation window. All are existing apparatus families; this is development evidence.
model_identity: gpt-6-luna is requested through the existing subscription provider. Usage metadata repeating that name does not independently establish server routing.
calibration_change: The fourth case starts with changed response parameters and keeps the same finite-history instrument. At the first trajectory starting at or after 96 paid rows the response parameters change again. The checkpoint and settled-state prediction objective are public; parameter values remain private.
learning: Start from the exact earlier selective source, retaining its working branches. Supply its actual paid case_3 failure using the existing counterexample interface. The author chooses all source edits and practice. No repaired branch is supplied.
publication: All four current-source cases must confirm, with unchanged-prior reuse and revision. Also demonstrate zero-measurement refit confirmation, and recovery after a validation-supported refit fails fresh confirmation, in different cases.
transfer: Freeze the published revision and run all eight registered targets against the exact earlier selective source, previous published source and developer controller. All four arms share priors, prefixes, actual laboratories and per-episode budgets. Transfer uses zero model calls. Without publication, keep revised slots skipped.
